newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Victoria launches 6 new gas companies.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Victoria launches 6 new gas companies.

text.p: The Victorian state government on Tuesday launched six new gas companies formed as a part of its plan to maximise competition within the state's gas retail and distribution industries.
The six new entities, three retailers and three distributors, will continue to operate as divisions of the state-owned GASCOR until they are fully corporatised in November.

"Today is another step towards this government's ultimate vision of an integrated energy market supplying both Victorian and Australian markets with low cost energy," Victoria's minister of finance Roger Hallam told the launch in Melbourne.
Hallam said the government's expectation was that all the new companies would be privatised by the end of calendar 1998.
The three retailers, Kinetic Energy, Energy 21 and Ikon Energy have been allocated customers in seperate geographical areas of the state in the lead up to next year's privitisation.

Hallam said from September next year, bulk users of gas would be able to shop around for the best deal and by 2001 all customers would be able to choose which company they purchased gas from on the basis of price and service.
Last week, the Victorian government legislated to cap the state's gas price rises at below the consumer price index rate until the period of full customer choice in 2001.
The three new gas distribution companies, Stratus Networks, Westar and Multinet would be responsible for delivering gas to consumers and connecting new customers to the gas pipeline.
While each retailer and distributor is responsible for supplying gas to a designated area of Victoria, these businesses would be allowed to compete for customers in 2001.
Hallam said a central services company had also been established to provide services to the gas retailers such as customer call centre, information technology and metering.
